sources.title: G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems (AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, online edition)
sources.locator: Section 2.1 (autonomous systems); Section 2.4, Theorem 2.10 and estimate (2.43) (smooth dependence and the first variational equation); Section 3.2 (the matrix exponential and linear systems); Section 6.1 (the flow and its cocycle identity); Section 6.4, Lemma 6.9 and the Poincare map (6.25); Sections 6.6-6.7 (Liapunov functions, Theorem 6.16); Sections 8.6 and 9.1-9.2 (harmonic modes, dichotomies, stable manifolds). Read in full at the cited sections from the local copy fetched by source-fetch-check.

contents.name: Section 2.1: autonomous systems and their maximal solutions, printed pp. 17-19
contents.support: The definition of the maximal solution family, the flow domain and the time-t maps follows this presentation with all domain conditions explicit.

contents.name: Section 6.1: the cocycle identity phi(t, phi(s,x)) = phi(t+s,x), printed pp. 190-192
contents.support: The identity, inverse-time law and the counterexample role of finite-time blow-up are exactly the three clauses proved in the lemma.

contents.name: Theorem 2.10 with estimate (2.43): C^k dependence on the initial condition and the first variational equation, printed pp. 45-48
contents.support: The trapping, Gronwall and variational-equation comparison steps follow this theorem, stated for C^1 fields with the explicit cylinder constants.

contents.name: Section 2.4: the flow domain and continuous dependence, printed pp. 45-48 and 190-192
contents.support: The open domain and C^1 regularity are assembled here from finitely many Picard-Lindelof steps.

contents.name: Section 6.4, Lemma 6.9 and the Poincare map (6.25), printed pp. 197-198
contents.support: The transversality hypotheses and the implicit-function construction of the local return map are the published treatment of this proposition, here carried out for the local flow with the reversed crossing.

contents.name: Section 9.1, Theorems 9.1-9.2 and formulas (9.2), (9.4), (9.6): exponential dichotomy estimates
contents.support: The invariant splitting and the four clauses of the dichotomy, including the polynomial factor for a Jordan block, follow this section with the constants computed in the Jordan-block example.

contents.name: Section 6.7, formula (6.47) and Theorem 6.16, printed pp. 203-209
contents.support: Energy as a constant of the motion and the local-minimum stability criterion are the published versions of the conservation lemma and the energy-stability theorem.

contents.name: Section 8.6, formulas (8.76)-(8.81): M q'' + W q = 0, the substitution (P,Q)=(V M^{1/2} p, V M^{-1/2} q) and the mode energies
contents.support: The decoupling transformation and modal-energy identities follow this section; the example of the spring chain is the source of the coupled-oscillator example.

contents.name: Section 9.2: stable and unstable manifolds of a hyperbolic fixed point, printed pp. 255-262
contents.support: Contextual cross-check of the instability and dichotomy contracts; no step is quoted from this section beyond the dichotomy restatement in Section 9.1.

contents.name: Problem 6.16 and Section 6.5 on stability of fixed points, printed pp. 198-200
contents.support: The x^2-family examples of Section 6.5 are the published background of the x^3 counterexample, which is verified directly in the item.

contents.name: Problem 6.14: the Poincare map of f(x,y)=(-y,x) for the section x>0, y=0
contents.support: The source exercise is the published model for the worked return map, which is recomputed from the explicit solution in the example.

contents.name: Section 9.1, formulas (9.3)-(9.4): the dichotomy constants C and c for the computed Jordan-block and diagonal examples
contents.support: The example recomputes e^{tA} and the estimates directly and checks the admissible constants C=1, c=1/2 and C=1, c=1/4.

sources.title: J. Arino, MATH 8430 Fundamental Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations (University of Manitoba), lecture notes
sources.locator: Section 1.3 (maximal solutions and gluing), Section 1.4 (continuous dependence and the variational equation), Appendix A.7 (Gronwall), Chapter 2 (flow differentiability and section maps). Read at the cited sections.

contents.name: Section 1.3: maximal solutions, gluing on overlapping intervals, printed pp. 22-28
contents.support: Independent treatment of the gluing argument used in the composition law.

contents.name: Section 1.4: continuous dependence on initial data, printed pp. 32-36
contents.support: Second treatment of the cylinder estimates, parallel to the Teschl argument.

contents.name: Section 1.4 and Chapter 2: differentiability of the flow and the variational equation, printed pp. 32-40 and 76-90
contents.support: Second treatment of the variational-equation identity and of section maps.

contents.name: Appendix A.7: the Gronwall inequality
contents.support: The quantitative form of Gronwall used in the estimates.

contents.name: Section 1.4: the variational equation for a linear system
contents.support: Contextual cross-check of the worked linear example.

sources.title: F. Ramponi, Notes on Lyapunov's theorem
sources.locator: Sections 2-4: the Lyapunov equation P = integral of e^{A^T t} Q e^{A t}, stability via linearisation, instability, and the x' = -x^2, x' = x^2 counterexamples on the final page. Read in full.

contents.name: Section 3: the Lyapunov matrix as an integral of e^{A^T t} e^{A t} and the equation A^T P + P A = -Q
contents.support: The construction of Q and the verification of the Lyapunov equation are exactly this argument.

contents.name: Section 4: instability when the linearisation has an eigenvalue with positive real part
contents.support: The indefinite-quadratic-form argument for instability is the published route followed by the theorem, with the hyperbolic hypothesis made explicit.

contents.name: Section 3: the Lyapunov equation as a second treatment of the dichotomy constants
contents.support: Independent cross-check for the computed constants.

contents.name: Final page: the counterexamples x' = -x^2 and x' = x^2 with vanishing linearisation
contents.support: The source exhibits the same phenomenon with x^2; the item records the x^3 variant with a complete direct refutation.

sources.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos, January 2015 version)
sources.locator: Sections 1.2.3 (energy conservation), 2.6 (small oscillations, eqs. (2.113)-(2.116)), 4.1 (the harmonic oscillator in phase space). Read at the cited sections.

contents.name: Section 1.2.3: energy conservation for a mechanical system, printed pp. 4-5
contents.support: Independent published treatment of the conservation identity, here generalised to a configuration-dependent C^2 metric.

contents.name: Section 2.6: normal modes of coupled oscillators and the mode frequencies, printed pp. 40-45
contents.support: Second treatment of the modal decoupling and the mode interpretation used in the coupled-oscillator example.

contents.name: Section 2.6: the second-order Taylor expansion of the potential at an equilibrium, printed pp. 37-40
contents.support: The small-oscillation linearisation context for the proposition; the item states the exact derivative computation itself.

contents.name: Section 2.6: higher-order terms and the approximation character of small oscillations, printed pp. 37-45
contents.support: Source for the scope warning that the linearisation is an approximation without a long-time error bound.

contents.name: Section 4.1: the harmonic oscillator in phase space, printed pp. 75-79
contents.support: Contextual cross-check of the worked oscillator example.

sources.title: C. Ulcigrai, MATH36206/MATHM6206 Topological and Symbolic Dynamics (University of Bristol/Manchester)
sources.locator: Sections 2.2-2.3 (definitions of transitivity, minimality, mixing and sensitivity), 2.6-2.7 (the bi-sided shift Sigma_N, the metric d_rho, cylinders and Theorem 2.7.1). Read at the cited sections.

contents.name: Definitions 2.2.2-2.2.4 and 2.3.4: topological transitivity, mixing, minimality and sensitive dependence
contents.support: The four-property vocabulary of the definition follows these standard formulations, including the uniform sensitivity constant.

contents.name: Section 2.7: the metrics d_rho on Sigma_N and Lemmas 2.7.1-2.7.3 identifying cylinders with balls
contents.support: The cylinder-ball comparison and the basis property follow this treatment for the two-symbol space.

contents.name: Section 2.6: periodic points of a shift of finite type (Corollary 2.6.1)
contents.support: Second treatment of density of periodic points for the full shift.

contents.name: Theorem 2.7.1: aperiodic topological Markov chains are topologically mixing
contents.support: The full two-symbol shift is the aperiodic one-state case; the item gives a direct cylinder proof.

contents.name: Sections 2.6-2.7: periodic sequences obtained by repeating a finite block
contents.support: The finite checks instantiate the source constructions on explicit words.

sources.title: E. Glasner and B. Weiss, Sensitive dependence on initial conditions (Nonlinearity 6, 1993, 1067-1075; updated author version)

contents.name: Section 0: transitivity, dense periodic points and sensitivity as a standard chaos package
contents.support: The stated-sense chaos definition records a chosen property package, with no claim about the word chaos in general.

contents.name: Section 2: sensitivity of subshifts of the two-symbol shift and compactness of subshifts
contents.support: Independent cross-check of compactness and the sensitivity constant for the full shift.

contents.name: Section 2: sensitivity of subshifts
contents.support: Second treatment of sensitivity; the item verifies it directly with constant 1.
